app.footer: Kawal Asap reads free public data: NASA FIRMS satellite detections, Open-Meteo air quality and wind, and OpenStreetMap tiles. Data availability varies by source and location, and this site is not an official product and not a warning service. For official advisories follow BMKG and the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre.

aqi.good.advice: Air is clean. No precaution needed.
aqi.good.do2: Open the windows while the air is like this.
aqi.good.do3: Watch the wind: haze can arrive from another province.
aqi.good.label: Good
aqi.hazardous.advice: Emergency conditions. Avoid outdoor activity entirely.
aqi.hazardous.do1: Stay indoors with the windows and doors closed.
aqi.hazardous.do2: Run an air purifier and avoid indoor smoke: cigarettes, candles, burning.
aqi.hazardous.do3: Get medical help for a heavy cough, breathlessness or chest pain.
aqi.hazardous.label: Hazardous
aqi.moderate.advice: Acceptable, though sensitive people may notice it.
aqi.moderate.do1: Sensitive groups can stay active, just ease off hard outdoor effort.
aqi.moderate.do2: Close the windows if you can see or smell smoke.
aqi.moderate.do3: Check this page again before outdoor plans.
aqi.moderate.label: Moderate
aqi.sensitive.advice: Children, older people and anyone with asthma or heart trouble should cut down outdoor effort.
aqi.sensitive.do1: Wear an N95 mask or equivalent if you are outside for long.
aqi.sensitive.do2: Children, older people and anyone with asthma are better off indoors.
aqi.sensitive.do3: Skip heavy outdoor exercise and field work.
aqi.sensitive.label: Unhealthy for sensitive groups
aqi.unhealthy.advice: Everyone should limit time outdoors and wear a mask if they must go out.
aqi.unhealthy.do1: Wear an N95 mask whenever you go outside.
aqi.unhealthy.do2: Keep windows and doors closed, run a purifier if you have one.
aqi.unhealthy.do3: Postpone outdoor activity, including exercise and field work.
aqi.unhealthy.label: Unhealthy
aqi.veryUnhealthy.advice: Stay indoors, close windows, run a filter if you have one.
aqi.veryUnhealthy.do1: Stay indoors unless you have to go out.
aqi.veryUnhealthy.do2: Wear an N95 mask even for a short trip.
aqi.veryUnhealthy.do3: With a heart or lung condition, contact a health service if you feel breathless.
aqi.veryUnhealthy.label: Very unhealthy

glossary.aqi.body: Air Quality Index on the US EPA scale, computed from the PM2.5 value. 0 to 50 is good, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 150 unhealthy for sensitive groups, and above 150 unhealthy for everyone.
glossary.aqi.label: AQI
glossary.confidence.body: How sure the satellite algorithm is that the hot pixel is a fire. Nominal is the normal band. Filtering to nominal and above drops the weakest signals.
glossary.confidence.label: Confidence
glossary.detection.body: One hot pixel seen by one satellite pass at one time. Two satellites can catch the same fire, and one large fire covers several pixels, so detections are not a count of fires.
glossary.detection.label: Detection
glossary.freshness.label: Freshness
glossary.frp.body: Fire radiative power, in megawatts: the energy the burning pixels give off. A higher value means a hotter, more intense burn, not a bigger area.
glossary.frp.label: FRP, radiative power
glossary.pm25.body: Particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres across, about a thirtieth of the width of a hair. They are small enough to reach the deepest parts of the lungs. Values here come from a model, not from a ground sensor.
glossary.pm25.label: PM2.5
glossary.risk.body: Our own heuristic, 0 to 100, blending how many detections were seen, how intense they are, the model PM2.5, rain in the last seven days and wind. A reading of the situation, never a forecast or an official warning.
glossary.risk.label: Risk score
glossary.unitPm.body: Micrograms of particles in one cubic metre of air, the standard way to express particle concentration. A clean day in Indonesia sits under about 20, and a bad haze day runs into the hundreds.
glossary.unitPm.label: µg/m³
guide.article.sourceNote: Reference material only: this site has not been reviewed or endorsed by these organisations.
guide.article.stepsNote: These are the same steps the site shows beside each index band, so this page and the number you looked at cannot disagree.
guide.children.intro: Children breathe more air per kilogram of body weight than adults and spend their day in groups, which is why the index bands treat them as needing extra care.
guide.children.know1Body: There is no feed of school closures or official notices here, and this is not an early warning service. Follow BMKG, your local government and your school for those announcements.
guide.children.know1Title: This site cannot tell you about your school
guide.children.know2Body: A single high hour is different from a week that stays high. The eight day track on a city page shows whether the value is settling or holding.
guide.children.know2Title: Watch the trend, not one reading
guide.children.quick: From the sensitive band upward, the useful change is less time outdoors and no hard outdoor exercise. Decisions about school belong to local authorities and the school; this site cannot make them for you.
guide.children.summary: Things families and caregivers may need to consider.
guide.children.title: Children and school
guide.data.intro: Two numbers sit side by side across this site and they are not the same kind of fact: a satellite detection and a modelled air value. Reading them as one score is where most confusion starts.
guide.data.know1Body: One hot pixel seen by one satellite pass at one time. Two satellites can catch the same fire, and one large fire covers several pixels, so detections are not a count of fires.
guide.data.know1Title: Detections are not a count of fires
guide.data.know2Body: The air index is computed from PM2.5 with the US EPA breakpoints instead of read from the provider's own index, and the regional risk score is our own heuristic, not an official warning and not a forecast.
guide.data.know2Title: The index here is derived, and we say so
guide.data.quick: A hotspot is a thermal anomaly seen from a satellite at one moment. An air value here is a model, not a measurement from a sensor near your house. They can be related, but one does not prove the other.
guide.data.step1: Read a detection count as activity. Say detections, never fires.
guide.data.step2: Check the timestamp on the panel you are reading. A value from yesterday is not today's air.
guide.data.step3: Compare the two numbers for the same place, and treat a match in time and location as a reason to look closer, never as proof.
guide.data.summary: What hotspots and air-quality readings actually tell you.
guide.data.title: Understanding the data
guide.disclaimer: This guidance is general information for the index bands shown on this site. It is not medical advice, it is not an official warning, and it has not been reviewed by a health authority. For local advice follow BMKG and your local health service.
guide.featuredText: Learn how to check air quality and decide what precautions may help.
guide.indoor.intro: Indoor air is mostly outdoor air plus whatever your own home adds, so the practical work is keeping smoke out and cooking smoke away from the room you are in.
guide.indoor.know1Body: An air cleaner works in the room it stands in, and it works best with that room closed up. There is no setting that keeps an entire house clean.
guide.indoor.know1Title: One room, not a whole house
guide.indoor.know2Body: Closing every window keeps heat in. In a hot room, open the far side briefly and close it again rather than leaving one window as a permanent vent.
guide.indoor.know2Title: Heat and smoke are two different problems
guide.indoor.quick: Close up when the air outside is worse than inside: windows and doors shut, gaps covered if you can, and ventilation saved for a moment when the reading improves. Sources of smoke inside, such as cigarettes, candles and burning, matter more than usual on those days.
guide.indoor.summary: Practical ways to reduce smoke entering your home.
guide.indoor.title: Indoor air
guide.masks.intro: A mask is a filter, and like any filter it only helps if it fits and if the air actually passes through it.
guide.masks.know1Body: A high rating on a mask that leaks around the nose does less than a lower rating that seals. If air escapes the edges when you breathe out, it will do the same when you breathe in.
guide.masks.know1Title: Fit decides more than the rating
guide.masks.know2Body: Wearing a mask does not make a bad air day harmless. The most useful protection is still spending less time in the smoke.
guide.masks.know2Title: A mask is not a substitute for time indoors
guide.masks.quick: For smoke and haze the useful choice is a well fitting N95 or equivalent respirator, worn so air passes through the filter rather than around its edges. A cloth or surgical mask is not designed for fine particles and does not remove them the way a respirator does.
guide.masks.summary: What masks can and cannot do to reduce particle exposure.
guide.masks.title: Choosing a mask
guide.outdoor.intro: Outdoor plans are a trade-off between what you need to do and what the air is like today. This page covers how to read that trade-off without overreacting to a single number.
guide.outdoor.know1Body: The air values on this site come from the CAMS global model at city points, so they describe the regional picture well and can miss a difference of a few streets. If you can see or smell smoke, treat that as information too.
guide.outdoor.know1Title: One number is a model, not your street
guide.outdoor.know2Body: Breathing rate decides how much of the air you take in. Walking is not the same as running, and an hour is not the same as ten minutes.
guide.outdoor.know2Title: Effort matters as much as the number
guide.outdoor.quick: Check the value for your place first, then match it to its band: below 50 is good and 51 to 100 is moderate, so outdoor plans can generally stand. Above 100, cut long outdoor effort and follow the mask advice for that band.
guide.outdoor.summary: How to think about outdoor activity when air quality is poor.
guide.outdoor.title: Going outside
guide.subtitle: Practical steps for understanding haze and reducing exposure when air quality is poor.
guide.symptoms.intro: This page is the shortest one on purpose. It diagnoses nothing, and it does not replace a health worker.
guide.symptoms.know1Body: The site measures nothing itself. It shows satellite detections and modelled values, so it cannot tell you how you feel or what is causing your symptoms.
guide.symptoms.know1Title: What this site measures, and what it does not
guide.symptoms.know2Body: Children, older people, anyone pregnant and anyone with asthma, heart or lung disease are the groups the index bands single out for extra care.
guide.symptoms.quick: Smoke and fine particles irritate the eyes, nose and throat and can make a cough or breathlessness worse, especially for anyone with asthma, a heart or lung condition, or during pregnancy. If symptoms feel heavy or do not ease, contact a health service rather than waiting for the air to improve.
guide.symptoms.summary: Warning signs and when to seek medical advice.
guide.symptoms.title: Symptoms and getting help
guide.title: Haze guide

method.air.gives: PM2.5, PM10, US AQI and European AQI for 35 Indonesian cities, hourly
method.air.licence: Free non-commercial use under CC BY 4.0
method.air.limits: Modelled concentrations from the CAMS global model, not ground stations. Good for the regional picture, less reliable for one street.
method.air.rhythm: Model output, refreshed hourly, 7 days of history available
method.costBody: All four data sources are free to read and need no paid subscription. Hosting is static files plus one serverless function, both inside a free tier. The site keeps its own caching in three layers, in the browser, at the edge and inside the function, so a busy day still means a small number of requests to NASA rather than one per visitor. The costs that would eventually appear are a custom domain and a proper map tile plan.
method.counter: The site also counts visits with GoatCounter. What is recorded is the page address and the time: no cookies, nothing that identifies a visitor, and nothing shared with an ad network. The address sent leaves out everything after the question mark, so your filters and the window you picked never leave the page.
method.firms.gives: Fire detections from VIIRS (Suomi NPP) and MODIS (Terra, Aqua)
method.firms.licence: Free US government data, credit NASA FIRMS
method.firms.limits: Detections, not fires. One burning area can appear in several passes and pixels. Small, short or smoky fires are missed, and the newest record lags real time by hours.
method.firms.rhythm: Near real time files, refreshed a few times an hour
method.forecast.gives: Wind at 10 m and 850 hPa on a 45 point grid, rain totals per region
method.forecast.licence: Free non-commercial use under CC BY 4.0
method.forecast.limits: Forecast model output, not observations. Useful for smoke transport direction, not a dispersion model.
method.geo.gives: Place names and coordinates, so air quality can be read anywhere
method.geo.limits: Settlement names only: what you type is matched to the nearest known place, not surveyed
method.introP1: Three questions drive the design: where are fires burning, what is the air like in the cities, and which way is the wind pushing the smoke. Every panel says where its numbers come from and when they were last updated, and a missing source is shown as missing instead of being drawn as zero.
method.introP2: It is not an official product, not an early warning service, and not a forecast. For advisories follow BMKG, the Ministry of Environment and the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre.
method.introSubtitle: A public interest reading of the haze situation in Indonesia, built only from free data.
method.limit1: Detections are countable events, so the same fire can be counted more than once across satellite passes. Read the numbers as activity, never as a count of fires.
method.limit2: There is no official Indonesian hotspot feed integrated here. BMKG publishes data, but its terms require using an official API, so this site does not scrape it.
method.limit3: Air quality and wind are model values, not station readings. OpenAQ would add real monitors but needs an API key and Indonesian coverage is thin.
method.limit4: Region grouping uses seven approximate boxes instead of province boundaries, and the boxes include a little neighbouring land. Fires outside every box are labelled neighbouring areas and kept out of the Indonesian totals.
method.limit5: There is no smoke dispersion model here. Wind arrows show which way the air is moving, and nothing more.
method.limit6: Hotspot history is limited to the seven days inside the NASA file. Longer trends need snapshots stored over time, which is the next thing to add.
method.limitsSubtitle: Read these before quoting a number.
method.mongabay.gives: Headlines, publishers and publication dates for reporting on fire, haze and air quality.
method.mongabay.licence: Free feed, no key. Reuse terms are the publisher own; only the headline, the date and a link are shown here.
method.mongabay.limits: One publisher, filtered to this subject. A story is tagged with a region only when the publisher own location metadata supports it, and the article is never reproduced. Their feed carries only the last twenty posts, so this is a window on recent reporting rather than an archive.
method.mongabay.rhythm: Publishes through the day; this site reads the feed at most every fifteen minutes.
method.nextSubtitle: The roadmap this version is built to grow into.
method.riskAirBody: : highest modelled PM2.5 among the region cities, saturating at 150 µg/m³.
method.riskBands: Bands: below 20 low, 20 to 39 moderate, 40 to 59 high, 60 and above very high. The national figure blends the worst region (weighted two thirds) with the average of all regions.
method.riskDispersionBody: : how light the wind is, because still air lets smoke linger, saturating below 18 km/h.
method.riskDryBody: : rain over the last seven days at the region centre, where 0 mm means maximum dryness and 60 mm or more means none.
method.riskFiresBody: : 24 hour detection count in the region, on a log scale that flattens out around 600 detections.
method.riskInspectable: Each region row lists the two or three signals that actually drove its score, so the number is never a black box.
method.riskIntensityBody: : mean fire radiative power of those detections, where 40 MW and above counts as the maximum.
method.riskNotForecast: The score is a summary of observed conditions and current weather. It does not predict tomorrow, and it is not comparable to an official air quality index.
method.riskSubtitle: Five signals, each turned into a 0 to 1 value, then weighted. Deliberately simple and inspectable.
method.riskTitle: How the haze risk score works
method.sourcesSubtitle: Five free sources, all attributed on this site.
method.step1: Store a daily snapshot so trends can run for months instead of eight days.
method.step2: Add province boundaries for administrative comparisons.
method.step3: Generate a plain language daily summary when something significant changes.
method.step4: Publish the aggregated JSON as a small public API for journalists and researchers.
method.tiles.gives: The base map, in both the dark and light styles
method.tiles.licence: OpenStreetMap data under ODbL, credit OpenStreetMap contributors
method.tiles.limits: The public tile server is meant for light use, so a busy site should move to its own tiles or a paid provider. The dark style is these same tiles passed through a CSS filter, not a separate product, and needs no account.

news.attributionNote: No headline, publisher or date on this site is invented, and nothing is shown until a source is real.
news.failedText: {publisher} answered with an error, so nothing is listed. An empty list would read as "no news", and a timed out request is not evidence of that.
news.failedTitle: The news feed could not be read
news.noItemsText: The feed was read and nothing in it is about fire, haze or air quality at the moment. The list stays short rather than filling with stories that are not about the subject.
news.sourceNote: Headlines, publishers and publication dates come from the {publisher} feed, and place tags come from the publisher own location metadata. Articles are never copied here: every item opens on the publisher site.
news.subtitle: Reporting on fires, haze and air quality from Indonesian publishers, each item linked to the original report.
news.title: News & developments
news.whySubtitle: One publisher feed is read, it is filtered to this subject, and the list stays empty when nothing relevant is published.
news.will1: The original headline, the publisher and the publication date, exactly as the publisher published them.
news.will2: A link that opens the publisher own page, where the article is complete. It opens in a new tab, and this site sends nothing with the request.
news.will3: No summary in our own words and no copy of the article, because the publisher terms do not allow it today. The row is the headline and the link.
news.will4: Only what is new. The publisher's feed carries their last twenty posts, so a report leaves this list as it rolls out of the feed, and the list stays short when little is being published.
